name: Delivery
blurb: How code reaches production, and how production reaches a human when it goes wrong. Nothing on this tab is on a user's request path.
note: Two of the paths drawn here do not work today. The canary's alarm has no alarm action, and the cross-region relay's inline handler has a syntax error, so the smoke test and every us-east-1 edge alarm currently notify nobody. Both are one-line fixes.

zones.label: Author and review · every pull request

d.role: Everything that runs before a change can merge.
facts: Four workflows fire on a pull request to main: Release Candidate (quality checks plus an ephemeral deploy), Validate OpenAPI Spec, Validate PR Title and, on close, Destroy Ephemeral Environment.

zones.label: Outside the pipeline · workspace, CLI and personal stages

d.role: What an engineer touches before a pull request exists.
One workflow run carries a commit from release to production.
facts: The spine down the middle is the only thing that blocks production; everything on the right rail runs beside it and gates nothing.

d.role: How a running stage reports on itself.
facts: Absorbed from the Containers view: these four AWS containers are operations, not part of the runtime request path.

d.role: Builds and deploys a domain. Writes no infrastructure.
facts: This is the intended operating model: a domain team is meant to own only domains/{name}/*. CODEOWNERS still assigns every path to the FLEX platform developers team pending domain-team onboarding.
Deploys by merging: the shared pipeline creates the Lambdas, API resources, IAM policies and alarms from the declared config.
Adding a domain needs no platform change; only a new third-party integration does.

dvla, example, groups and uns each take a workspace dependency on @flex/udp-domain; three of them import a udp Zod schema into their own domain.config.ts, so a udp schema change is a compile-time break.

d.role: Owns every piece of infrastructure a domain runs on.
facts: Owns libs/*, platform/* and the CDK app — and, until domain teams onboard, every path in CODEOWNERS as well.
Owns the two shared API Gateways, the VPC, the service gateways and the pipeline itself.
A domain team never writes CDK; the platform team never writes domain logic.

d.role: Hosts the code, the pipeline and the releases.
facts: Everything reaches production through one workflow: Continuous Deployment, on push to main.
Deployment credentials are never stored — CI federates into AWS with OIDC and a per-environment role.

d.role: Enforces the commit header that semantic-release later parses.
facts: Fails unless the title matches {JIRA-KEY} {type}(scope)?!?: description, with type one of feat, fix, chore, docs, style, refactor, test, perf, ci, build or revert.
The squash-merge commit is this title, and the release parser tolerates a leading Jira key — the gate is what makes that tolerance safe rather than accidental.
Dependabot pull requests are skipped; a single bot comment is created or updated with the guidance.

d.role: The pull-request event that starts the checks below.
facts: Release Candidate runs Quality Checks and the ephemeral deploy in parallel, then Module E2E against the stage it created.
Concurrency is grouped per head ref: the OpenAPI and title workflows cancel in-progress runs, Release Candidate deliberately does not.

d.role: Hygiene, SonarQube and Security, on pull requests and on main alike.
facts: Hygiene: pre-commit over all files, then lint, tsc and validate:integrations.
Security: checkov over synthesised CloudFormation, plus dependency review failing at high severity.
Nx runs lint, tsc and checkov against affected projects, on PR and main runs alike; unit tests always run for every project (run-many --all) inside the SonarQube job.
Only the CDK app declares a checkov target, so that scan runs only when platform/infra is affected.

d.role: Regenerates every domain's spec and diffs it against what is published.
facts: oasdiff compares against the specs in the development spec bucket — not staging, not production.
Only ERR-level findings fail; a spec that disappears counts as breaking too.
The breaking-change-accepted label overrides the failure.

d.role: A complete, isolated copy of the platform for one pull request.
facts: Reuses the development VPC, endpoints, security groups and alarm topics — it creates no core stack, and no canary.
Environment gating is only enforced for persistent stages, so every domain deploys here, example included.
It runs the same reusable job as the three environments, Platform E2E included, and gets its own subdomain and its own WAF bypass secret.

d.role: Static analysis across the whole workspace; coverage across the domains, libs and service gateways only — the CDK app, CLI, testing lib, smoke-test, domain.config.ts/gateway.config.ts files, example and local-council are all excluded from coverage.
facts: sonar.qualitygate.wait=true, so a failing gate fails the job.
It also consumes an ESLint JSON report, generated with || true so a lint crash cannot fail the scan.

d.role: Runs each domain's own E2E suite against the ephemeral stage.
facts: Domains are discovered at runtime by scanning for a test:e2e script — five of six qualify; local-council declares none, so it is never covered.
fail-fast is off, so one domain failing does not mask the others.
Suites read their URLs from the FlexPlatform and FlexGlobal stack outputs rather than hard-coding them.

d.role: Tears the ephemeral stage down when the pull request closes.
facts: The ephemeral OpenAPI specs bucket is created with autoDeleteObjects so the destroy completes; the two access-log buckets it depends on are object-locked (365-day GOVERNANCE) and retained.

d.role: Scaffolds a whole domain from templates.
facts: Eight Mustache templates produce package.json, domain.config.ts, tsconfig, vitest and eslint config, a README and one v1/hello handler.
It then runs pnpm up --latest, pnpm install, tsc and lint inside the new package, so a scaffolded domain compiles before anything is written by hand.
This is the on-ramp that makes "adding a domain needs no platform change" true.

d.role: A full named stage an engineer deploys from a laptop.
facts: getEnvConfig() falls back to process.env.USER, so a deploy with no STAGE set creates a stage named after the engineer — lowercased, stripped to a-z0-9- and truncated to 12 characters.
It behaves exactly like a PR stage: development account, development VPC, endpoints and topics, every domain including example.
Nothing tears it down — only pr-{number} stages have a cleanup workflow.

d.role: What is allowed into the dependency tree and the working tree.
facts: pnpm minimumReleaseAge: 10080 quarantines any newly published version for seven days.
An overrides block pins six transitive dependencies out of vulnerable ranges; allowBuilds denies install scripts by default, permitting only esbuild and the Playwright Chromium browser.
pre-commit runs Yelp detect-secrets against a 129KB checked-in baseline, plus detect-private-key and the file hygiene hooks — CI runs the same hooks with --all-files.
Dependabot batches patch and minor updates weekly for npm and GitHub Actions, with a 7-day cooldown.

d.role: Decides the version and publishes the release notes.
facts: The commit parser tolerates a leading Jira key, so FLEX-250 chore: … still classifies correctly.
Tags are v{version}; when nothing is released the run falls back to the latest tag, then to the short SHA, so a deployment notice always names something.
Only major and minor releases publish a Slack notice, and that step is continue-on-error.

d.role: How CI gets into the accounts.
facts: A separate role secret per environment — DEV, STAGING and PROD; the ZAP scan and a staging performance run assume the staging one too.
Short-lived credentials only; nothing long-lived is stored in GitHub.
The session name is the workflow run ID, so CloudTrail ties every action back to a run.
The staging role's trust policy only allows main, which is why the ZAP runbook says to swap in the dev role when testing from a branch.

d.role: Supplies the hosted zone, auth identifiers and consumer secrets.
facts: Declared through addExternalExports: importing a key no stack exports and that isn't declared external fails the synth. The values themselves are CloudFormation SSM references resolved at deploy time, so a parameter missing from SSM fails the deploy.
The only genuine synth-time read is ReleaseSlackChannelId, via valueFromLookup.
One import escapes the rule: the Lambda environment-encryption CMK is read with valueForStringParameter without being declared external, so a missing key there surfaces at deploy rather than synth.

d.role: Turns SSM imports and exports into stack dependencies.
facts: Every import() records an edge and willCreateCycle rejects a cycle at synth; synth() then converts each edge into an addDependency call.
That ordering is what makes cdk deploy --all --concurrency 4 safe.

Stacks per stage: FlexCore and FlexSmokeTest (persistent stages only), FlexPlatform, FlexGlobal in us-east-1, one stack per deployable domain, and FlexApiDeployment last. FlexMacie is commented out in app.ts.

d.role: Forces a new deployment of both REST APIs once the domain stacks have added their routes.
facts: It declares every deployed domain stack as a dependency, which is how the graph places it last.
The sorted METHOD:path list is SHA-256 hashed into the deployment description, so a redeploy only happens when the route set actually changes.
A CfnPause custom resource sleeps six seconds between the public and the private call, because createDeployment is rate-limited.

d.role: Generate OpenAPI, cdk deploy --all, then Platform E2E.
facts: pnpm openapi:generate runs first, so the specs ship with the deploy.
cdk deploy --all --concurrency 4 --require-approval never.
Platform E2E runs inside this job, so a failure blocks promotion.

d.role: Domain suites against the development stage.
facts: A separate job that needs deployDev — and so does the staging deploy, so staging can start while these are still running.

d.role: A human must approve before staging.
facts: Configured on the GitHub environment the reusable deploy job names, not in the workflow file.
The first of two independent approvals.

d.role: The same reusable job, with the staging stage and role.
facts: Platform E2E runs here too, and a failure blocks production.

d.role: Domain suites against staging.
facts: deployProd needs only deployStaging, so these suites run alongside the production gate rather than before it.

d.role: Publishes the staging deployment notice.
facts: Assumes the development role, because the release topic only exists in the development account.
Both steps are continue-on-error — a failed notification must never fail the pipeline.

d.role: A second human approval before production.
facts: Independent of the staging approval — approving one does not approve the other.

d.role: The same job once more.
facts: Platform E2E is skipped in production, and no Module E2E runs against it.
Production correctness therefore rests on staging plus the always-on canary, whose alarm currently notifies nobody.

d.role: Publishes the production deployment notice.
facts: A separate failure notification fires if any stage's deploy job fails, naming the first stage that failed.

d.role: Dynamic security scan driven by an OpenAPI document.
facts: Triggered by workflow_run when the whole Continuous Deployment workflow completes successfully on main — including the production gate. If production is rejected, DAST never runs.
Mints a real JWT first; the scan emits a SARIF report kept as a workflow-run artifact — nothing uploads it to code scanning.

The target is .zap/merged-openapi.json, a spec committed with the workflow and unchanged since: paths such as /v1/driving-licence and /v1/customer-summary no longer exist, and .zap/rules.tsv is empty.

d.role: Load profiles against a deployed stage.
facts: Six profiles live in tests/performance — smoke, load-baseline, load-growth, spike, stress (ramping to 2000 virtual users) and soak — but the workflow runs only the three default scenarios, one job each.
Thresholds are declared per scenario (p95 3000ms for the upsert, 1500ms for the two reads, error rate under 1%) and the run step is continue-on-error, so a breach never fails the workflow.
On staging every virtual user shares one real Cognito token, so those numbers measure endpoint throughput, not per-user concurrency.
The user-settings scenario PATCHes /app/udp/v1/users/notifications, but the udp route is /v1/users/me/notifications — it cannot return the 200 it asserts.

d.role: Synthetic canary exercising the whole public path.
facts: Calls GET /app/udp/v1/users/me through the public URL, so CloudFront, the edge function, WAF, the certificate, the authorizer and the udp domain are all covered by one signal.
Publishes Flex/SmokeTest.SmokeTestSuccess as 1 or 0 — but its alarm has no SNS action, so nothing is notified.

Credentials differ by environment: a self-signed stub token in development, a real One Login sign-in with e-mail, password and TOTP in staging and production, and a Firebase App Check header everywhere except staging.
Persistent stages only, production included — which makes it the second production caller of the public path.

d.role: Mints the attestation token the canary attaches.
facts: No stored key: an external account client exchanges a federated credential for a GCP token, then Firebase App Check mints the header.
Used only by the canary — it is not on any user request path.

d.role: Lambda, API Gateway, CloudFront, edge functions, WAF, Shield and the canary.
facts: Every alarm routes to exactly one of two SNS topics, critical or warning — except the canary's {stage}-smoke-test-no-success alarm, which currently has no alarm action wired.
Descriptions start with Critical: or Warning: and state the breached condition, so the Slack message alone usually picks the runbook.
The four families created in us-east-1 can only reach Slack through the relay.

d.tech: SNS → Lambda → SNS, one shared KMS key
d.role: Republishes us-east-1 alarms onto the eu-west-2 topics — currently non-functional.
facts: Lives in us-east-1: CloudWatch cannot target an SNS topic in another region, so edge alarms need this hop to reach the eu-west-2 topics.

TopicArn: ${targetTopicArn} is interpolated unquoted into Code.fromInline, so the handler is a JavaScript syntax error and fails on every invocation. Every CloudFront, edge-function, CLOUDFRONT-scope WAF and Shield alarm therefore reaches nobody. The REGIONAL WAF alarms publish straight to the eu-west-2 topics and are unaffected.
Passes through message and message attributes; truncates the subject to 100 characters.
#buildRelay is called twice, once per severity, so there are two topics and two functions sharing one relay key.

d.role: flex-alerts-critical and flex-alerts-warning, plus the release topic.
facts: Created by the core stack, so they exist only in persistent stages; ephemeral and personal stages import the development ones.
flex-release-notifications exists only in development, which is why the staging and production notify jobs assume the development role to publish.

d.role: Delivers alarms to Slack via the flex-alerts-{stage} channel configuration; the target channel comes from the MonitoringSlackChannelId parameter.
facts: A ReadOnlyAccess guardrail policy caps what anyone can do from Slack.
Development adds one more configuration per release channel ID, and those IDs are the one value read at synth time.

d.role: Where alarms and deployment notices land.
facts: flex-alerts-{stage} for alarms; separate release channels, in development only, for deployment and release notices.

d.role: Responds to alarms.
facts: The Slack message carries the severity and the breached condition, which is usually enough to pick a runbook without opening the console.

d.role: Written procedures for what fires.
facts: Eight runbooks: API Gateway 5xx, Lambda errors and throttling, external service outage, leaked secret, fix-forward, pipeline promotion, deploying to staging/production, and environment health.
This is how a domain is deployed — there is no separate domain deployment path.

d.carries: libs/*, platform/* and the CDK app
facts: A platform change can alter every domain's infrastructure at once, which is why the pipeline gates on Platform E2E.

edges.label: gates what can enter the tree

d.carries: Secret scanning, dependency quarantine and pinning

edges.label: on pull_request · opened, edited, synchronize, reopened

facts: Quality Checks run again on main before the release job.
Runs in parallel with Quality Checks, not after it.

d.carries: Test coverage for every project and an ESLint report

d.auth: Self-signed stub JWT plus the x-flex-e2e-bypass WAF header
facts: The bypass header value is a per-stage Secrets Manager secret; it skips the WAF's IP-reputation rule, nothing else.
A newly scaffolded domain reaches a running stage without any platform change — the claim on the left, made concrete.
Each of the three deploy jobs assumes its own role; the ephemeral and personal stages use the development one.

d.carries: Hosted zone, auth IDs, consumer secret ARNs
facts: Each persistent stage reads its own /{environment}/… parameters; ephemeral and personal stages fall back to the development environment's values.
Imported outside the dependency graph, because another repository owns their lifecycle.
A Platform E2E failure in development stops the pipeline here.

edges.label: after the whole Continuous Deployment run succeeds

facts: The trigger is the workflow, not the staging deploy: the run has to clear the production gate first, so a rejected production deploy means no DAST at all.
Published to the development account's release topic, and delivered by a separate Chatbot configuration to the release channels — not to flex-alerts.
Only major and minor releases also produce a release notice.

d.auth: Role scoped to the Flex/SmokeTest namespace
facts: Missing data is treated as breaching, so a canary that stops running would still alarm — if the alarm had an action.

d.carries: CloudFront, edge function, CLOUDFRONT-scope WAF and Shield alarms
facts: CloudWatch cannot target a topic in another region, which is the only reason this hop exists.
Broken today: the handler fails to parse, so nothing is republished.

tables.name: Every alarm, its threshold, and which topic it reaches
rows: Blocked requests, anomaly detection at 2 std devs
tables.note: 18 alarms from six constructs in constructs/alarms/. Every one sets treatMissingData: NOT_BREACHING, so silence never fires an alarm. Critical and Warning are two separate SNS topics, wired in constructs/alarms/actions.ts. The CloudFront, CloudFront Function and Shield rows are measured in us-east-1, because that is the only region those metrics are emitted to — they reach the eu-west-2 topics through the cross-region relay.
